commands.description: Snapshot of OrcaSlicer. Call it first and whenever you are unsure what the app is doing. The app: version, platform and display backend, whether it is ready, the main window, the displays (each one's work area x, y, width and height, as set_window takes positions, its scale and whether it is primary), the MCP endpoint (mcp), python (available: Python runs in this build; scripts_unrestricted: a script's own file, network, process and thread access is not held to OrcaSlicer's folders, which only a person turns on, in Preferences > AI features > Python scripts), design_tab (the Design tab is on, and call_tool runs its commands, search_tools' group Design) and, when they do not run, cad_note, how a person turns the CAD feature on. The project: current tab and mode, printer technology, name, path and unsaved changes, selected printer/process/filament presets, plates (count, current), object count, the selection (objects, the instances [[object, instance]] they are selected in and, when parts rather than whole instances are selected, parts [[object, part]], in the indices select_objects takes; wipe_tower when a prime tower is selected; canvas is the 3D view it belongs to), slicing state, the Preview's view type, time mode and layer range (1-based, with their Z), and the camera of the 3D view shown (camera: type, look_at, position, zoom, click_px_per_mm, elevation and azimuth, as set_view replies with it). What is going on: open modal dialogs, each with its title, buttons (enabled: false when disabled) and a message that reads it as shown: its text and its controls row by row, fields [value], choices [value ▾], checkboxes [x] / [ ] / [-], radio and selector options (*) / ( ), list rows "- row | cells", secrets [******], " (disabled)" after a disabled control; menus closed unseen (a menu a call opened that no reply listed), auto_answer_dialogs rules in force, notifications, print host uploads (state, progress, error), the open gizmo, running jobs and a running recording.

commands.description: Find what does something, in one search, or look up one command. With query: the commands that match, best first, each with its group, the first sentence of its description and listed, whether the tool list shows it; one that is not listed (a Speed Dial command, a Design tab command, or an operation a plugin offers, plugin.<plugin>.<name>) comes with its input schema, and its description when that says more, which nothing else shows. Beside them, the best few matches of each other catalog, with its total and how to use it: actions (the Speed Dial's plates, recent projects and plugin scripts and pages, for run_action), settings (get_settings / set_settings) and python (the orca API for run_script). With tool: that command's description and input schema, and its examples when it has some (the Design commands do). With neither: every command's name. group keeps the names and the command matches to one group; the other catalogs' matches stay as they are. call_tool runs any command, listed or not.

A group no command has is refused with the groups there are.

With arguments, or silent: true, it asks nothing: it fails, changing nothing, when the current project has unsaved changes, unless discard_changes. The presets' unsaved changes carry over to the new project unless preset_changes is "discard", as New Project's prompt offers. Reply: objects, names, plates; when presets had or have unsaved changes, discarded and modified list per preset the keys dropped and the keys still unsaved.

discard_changes.description: Drop the project's unsaved changes rather than fail; for the presets', see preset_changes.

commands.description: Generate a Calibration menu test as its dialog's OK does: a new project named after the test with the test model, and the process, filament and printer presets changed as the test needs (presets_changed). The test prints with filament slot 1, so the filament tab is pointed at slot 1's preset. Omitted parameters take the dialog's defaults (pressure advance's by the printer's extruder type); temperatures are clamped to 155-500 °C and rounded down to 5 °C. Fails, changing nothing, when the project has unsaved changes (pass discard_changes) or presets do (pass preset_changes). Reply: test, project, params (the values used, which the journal records), objects, names, plates, presets_changed, result_keys (where the measured value belongs), warnings, adjusted (vfa), and discarded and modified as new_project. Then slice and export. To save a measured value: new_project {discard_changes, preset_changes: "discard"}, set_settings the value, save_preset.

accelerations.description: pressure_advance pattern: one test per acceleration and speed; default the process's.

auto_adjust.description: vfa: lower the layer height, else the end speed, to stay within the filament's maximum volumetric speed (default true).

auto_scale.description: temperature, vfa: scale the model to the nozzle (default true).

damping.description: input_shaping_freq: the damping ratio printed with.

discard_changes.description: Drop the project's unsaved changes rather than fail; for the presets', see preset_changes.

end_y.description: input_shaping_freq: end of the Y range; default the X one.

freq_y.description: input_shaping_damp: the Y frequency, Hz; default freq_x.

method.description: pressure_advance: tower (default), line or pattern; flow_ratio: pass1, pass2, yolo (default) or yolo_perfectionist.

preset_changes.description: The presets' unsaved changes, not the project's: keep them for the test or drop them first. Required when presets are modified.

print_numbers.description: pressure_advance line: print the values (default true).

shaper_type.description: Input shaping: an input_shaping_type the printer's firmware offers; default the first.

speeds.description: pressure_advance pattern: default an optimal speed.

commands.description: Save the project. Called with no arguments, it saves as Save Project does: to the project's file, or, when it has none, through a file dialog (blocked_by_dialog; a native picker needs auto_answer_dialogs registered first). With path, it saves a .3mf there without a dialog, and the file becomes the project's.

path.description: Absolute .3mf path.

silent.description: true runs the command without asking, with the defaults of what the call leaves out. A call with no arguments does what a person's pick does.

commands.title: Save Project

commands.description: Printer, process or filament presets with flags: system or user, selected (and modified), compatible with the selected printer, and for filaments the slots using them. Only compatible, visible presets unless asked: a fresh install hides most system filaments and printers (visible: false), and select_preset takes those too.

include_incompatible.description: Also list presets incompatible with the printer.

commands.title: List presets

commands.description: Select a printer, process or filament preset by the name its selector shows (or its internal name), as a person would. A hidden one (list_presets include_hidden) is shown in the selectors first, until the app restarts. With unsaved changes the Transfer-or-discard prompt opens (blocked_by_dialog) unless preset_changes answers it. A filament is assigned to filament_slot (1-based, default 1). Reply: selected, shown (a hidden preset it showed); when presets had or have unsaved changes, discarded and modified list per preset the keys dropped and the keys still unsaved.

name.description: Preset name as list_presets shows it.

preset_changes.description: Unsaved changes of the presets the switch replaces: move them to the new preset or drop them, as the prompt's buttons do. Omitted: the prompt opens.

commands.title: Select a preset

commands.description: Save the printer, process or filament preset being edited, with its unsaved changes, as a preset called name, which is then selected: what the tab's Save button does through its dialog. A filament is filament_slot's (default 1), and every slot using the old preset takes the new one. Replacing another existing preset needs overwrite (pass it in replays and scripts meant to be rerun). Reply: saved, user, project, inherits, filament_slots. A temperature warning or an unsaved-changes prompt makes it blocked_by_dialog. To keep only some edits, set_settings {reset_all: true, values} first.

detach.description: Copy inherited values and drop the parent (Developer mode).

inside_project.description: Keep it inside the project, not as a user preset. Default: where the edited preset is.

overwrite.description: Replace another preset of that name.

commands.title: Save a preset

commands.description: Delete a user preset or one inside the project, its file and its cloud copy, as the tab's Delete does, without asking. A selected preset is replaced as the tab does (its parent or the next preset). Another filament is deleted without changing the selection, and slots using it take the selected one; another process is selected, deleted and the selection restored; a printer must be selected first. Refused: system presets, presets others inherit from, another preset while the edited one of its type has unsaved changes. Deleting a selected printer or process can ask about other presets' unsaved changes (blocked_by_dialog). Reply: deleted, selected, filaments (per slot), attached, and discarded/modified as select_preset's.

delete_attached.description: A custom printer: also delete the process and filament presets made for it alone, which the GUI deletes with it.

name.description: Preset name as list_presets shows it.

commands.title: Delete a preset

commands.description:
Read settings: each item has its value, as OrcaSlicer writes it, and meta: label, description (what the setting does, when to change it), where (its settings page and group), type, unit, range, allowed values and mode. Choose them by keys; by query, a few words matched in keys, labels and descriptions, best matches first; by where, a page or group (an unknown one lists them all); or by none of these, for the whole scope, paged and, in a preset scope, without meta. Keys the scope lacks are listed in unknown_keys, and scope_of gives the scope of those another scope has.
- No scope: keys and query look through the process, filament and printer settings, and each item names its scope, the one set_settings takes; anything else reads the process.
- process, filament, printer: the preset being edited, or with preset a saved one; compare lists only the keys that differ from another preset (value and other). A per-variant value lists in meta its variants (what each entry is for) and active (the entry each extruder prints with).
- object, part: the overrides that object or part carries, each with effective (the value it prints with) and source (part, object, process or default); an object's item lists in parts the parts and modifiers that override the key inside their own volume.
- project: the plate type, slot colours, flushing volumes, purge mode, prime tower position per plate, mixed slots and, with several extruders, the filament grouping; meta.offered lists the choices this printer has.
- plate: a plate's curr_bed_type, print_sequence, spiral_mode, first_layer_print_sequence, other_layers_print_sequence, name and locked, each with value (the plate's own, null where it follows the global setting or Auto) and effective.
- preferences: the named keys of the app configuration (the Preferences dialog's settings, keys as its controls are named), as stored; it lists none unasked.

compare.description: Preset scopes: a preset name, ":saved" (the unsaved changes) or ":parent" (the preset it inherits from).

include_meta.description: Include labels, types and ranges. Default true, false for a preset scope's whole listing and with compare.

plate.description: Plate index (plate scope; default: the current plate).

preset.description: Preset scopes: read this saved preset (a name from list_presets) instead of the one being edited.

query.description: A few distinctive words, e.g. "stringing" or "ooze travel"; the best 20 matches unless limit says otherwise.

scope.description: Which settings: the process, filament or printer preset being edited, an object's / part's own overrides, the project's own settings, a plate's, or the app's preferences (read only). Without it, keys and query look through the process, filament and printer settings; anything else reads the process.

where.description: A settings page, or "Page > Group" as meta.where gives it, e.g. "Strength > Walls".

commands.title: Read settings

commands.description:
Change settings of one scope (default the process) as typing them into its settings tab would. Values are strings in OrcaSlicer's format ("15%", "0.2", "1,2") or JSON numbers, booleans and arrays (a point as [x, y]). All are parsed strictly first and applied together, so nothing changes if one is invalid, and a key of another scope is refused with that scope named. Reply: applied, and changed, every setting the call changed, including those the app adjusted in turn. One undo step. Spiral vase and a few others confirm their adjustments in a dialog (blocked_by_dialog).
- process, filament, printer: null takes a key back to its saved value, or with reset_to parent to the parent's; reset_all first discards every unsaved change, as the tab's undo button does (reply: reverted). A per-variant value (get_settings meta.variants) takes one value for the entries in use (meta.active), {index, value} for one entry, or an array of all.
- object, part: overrides of the keys the object list offers there; null removes one. extruder is the object's or part's filament (1-based; 0 or null for Default), set as the Change Filament menu does.
- project, as the sidebar's controls write them: curr_bed_type, filament_colour (#RRGGBB per slot), flush_multiplier, flush_volumes_matrix, prime_volume_mode, and wipe_tower_x/y (mm from the plate's origin, one per plate). flush_volumes_matrix is per nozzle, slots x slots from row to column, in config order over every slot, before the multiplier; mixed slots' entries are left as they are, and a colour change can recalculate it, so set it last.
- plate, which it selects and writes as the Plate Settings dialog's OK does: curr_bed_type, print_sequence ("by layer", "by object"), spiral_mode (true asks for confirmation), first_layer_print_sequence (every slot once, e.g. [2, 1]), other_layers_print_sequence ([{from: layer >= 2, to, order}], to omitted for the last layer), name and locked; null returns a value to the global setting or Auto.

object_id.description: The id list_objects reports for this object: the call is refused when the index names another one now.

part_id.description: The id list_objects reports for this part: the call is refused when the index names another one now.

plate.description: Plate index (plate scope; default: the current plate).

reset_all.description: Preset scopes: discard the unsaved changes before applying values.

reset_to.description: Preset scopes: what a null value takes a key back to: the saved preset (default) or the preset it inherits from.

scope.description: Which settings: the process, filament or printer preset being edited, an object's / part's own overrides, the project's own settings, a plate's, or the app's preferences (read only). Default: the process.

values.description: {key: value}, or {key: {index, value}} for one entry

commands.title: Change settings

commands.description: Plates with name, locked, current, objects (how many are on it; list_objects lists them), and the settings they print with: curr_bed_type, print_sequence, spiral_mode, first_layer_print_sequence and other_layers_print_sequence (null: Auto); overrides lists those the plate sets itself (set_settings scope plate). Also sliced (an up-to-date slice), wipe_tower [x, y] and layer_gcode: the plate's pauses, custom G-code, templates and filament changes, each {z, layer, type, filament, color, gcode}; layer is the Preview slider's number, given while the plate's slice is up to date.
commands.title: List plates

commands.description: The project as the Objects panel lists it. plates: each {index, name, objects}, with the objects that have an instance on it; outside: the objects with an instance on no plate. An object with instances on two plates is listed under both, each time with that plate's instances. An object has its filament, auto_drop, bounding box (instance 0), brim ear count and the settings it overrides; its instances (offset, rotation in degrees, scale, mirrored, bbox); its parts, one or more: parts, negative parts, modifiers, support blockers and enforcers and precise seams (type, with subtype for a precise seam; filament: a part's own or its object's, a modifier's only when it sets one; position, bbox and scaled_volume in mm3 on the bed, measured on instance 0; rotation_deg and scale in the object's frame; mirrored; triangle count; mesh_volume, the unscaled mesh's mm3; painted facets: supports and seam enforcers/blockers, fuzzy_skin, mmu per filament, texture per layer; a text part's text and font, an SVG part's file); its height range modifiers when it has any (layer_config_ranges: [{min_z, max_z, values}], as set_height_ranges takes them) and its variable layer height profile when it has one (layer_height_profile: {points, min_height, max_height}). A bbox is {min, max, size} in mm of model parts only, so unlike the panel's Size it leaves out modifiers. An object's index numbers it in the project and a part's in its object, whatever the plate: they are what select_objects, transform, mouse_gesture targets and the object/part settings scopes take. Each object and part also has an id, which stays with it when a delete, split or assemble shifts the indices: pass it as object_id / part_id to transform, add_part, set_settings, set_height_ranges and set_variable_layer_height (object_ids, part_ids and instance_object_ids to select_objects), and a call whose index names another one now is refused instead of acting on it. limit and offset page the objects and total counts them, each once.

plate.description: List this plate alone, without outside.

screen.description: Add each instance's rectangle in the shown 3D view, logical pixels [x, y, w, h].

commands.title: List objects

commands.description: Select objects, instances or parts in the 3D view (the assemble view while it is shown, else Prepare, switching to it), as clicking them would. Give objects, instances ([[object, instance], ...]) or parts ([[object, part], ...]); add keeps the current selection; all / none select everything or nothing. The reply is the selection as get_app_state.selection gives it.

add.description: Add to the selection instead of replacing it.

instance_object_ids.description: The ids list_objects reports for the objects of instances, one per entry: refused when a pair names another object now.

object_ids.description: The ids list_objects reports for objects, one per entry: refused when an index names another object now.

part_ids.description: The ids list_objects reports for the entries of parts, one per entry: refused when a pair names another part now.

commands.title: Select objects

commands.description: Change one instance's placement, or one part's with part. translate is in mm, position where it goes (mm, as the Move panel shows it, whatever mode says), rotate in degrees about X/Y/Z, scale a factor (one number or [x, y, z]), size [x, y, z] mm along the object's or part's own axes, plate moves the instance onto that plate at the same place. mode "relative" (default) adds to the current placement, "absolute" sets it. An instance is dropped back onto the bed unless drop_to_bed is false. A part moves as the Object manipulation panel moves it: translate and rotate along the bed's axes, measured on instance 0, scale and size along its own axes; every instance shows the change, and Auto Drop may lower the object afterwards. One undo step. Reply: the instance's offset, scale and plate, or the part's size along its own axes and its list_objects entry (part_info).

object_id.description: The id list_objects reports for this object: the call is refused when the index names another one now.

part.description: Transform this part instead of the instance.

part_id.description: The id list_objects reports for this part: the call is refused when the index names another one now.

plate.description: Move the instance to this plate.

position.description: [x, y, z] mm: the position to move to. Not with translate.

rotate.description: [x, y, z] degrees; relative only for a part

size.description: [x, y, z] mm, null keeps an axis; one number and two nulls keep the proportions. Not with scale.

commands.title: Move, rotate or scale an instance or a part

commands.description: Add a part, negative part, modifier, support blocker or enforcer, or precise seam to an object, as its context menu's Add items do: a primitive shape at a size, or a model file as Load... adds it. The part lands where the menu puts it (a shape beside the object, a file at its coordinates relative to the object's first part) unless position is given. Like the menu, adding a shape folds the instance's rotation and scale into the object's parts (the instance's scale then reads 1). Refused for an object with several instances: add parts first. A STEP file may ask for mesh options (blocked_by_dialog). The new part is selected; one undo step. Reply: its index, which is not always the last (parts are ordered by type), the object's part count and the part's list_objects entry (part_info).

object_id.description: The id list_objects reports for this object: the call is refused when the index names another one now.

path.description: Instead of shape: absolute path of a model file (STL, OBJ, 3MF, STEP, ...).

position.description: [x, y, z] mm on the bed for the part's centre, on instance 0, as the Move panel shows it.

size.description: mm, the Primitive size dialog's fields: cube [x, y, z]; cylinder, cone, disc [diameter, height]; sphere [diameter]; torus [inner diameter, tube diameter]. Default: the built-in size.

commands.title: Add a part or modifier to an object

commands.description: Arrange the objects of every unlocked plate as the toolbar's Arrange does, or of one plate (plates: an index or "current") as its Arrange icon does. With fill, fill that object's plate with more of it instead, as Fill bed with instances (or copies, by fill_with) does. spacing, rotate, align_y and multi_material are the Arrange options panel's settings: the values given stay in the panel, so later arranges use them too. Waits for the arrangement (a longer one replies with a job). Reply: the settings in force, instances left off every plate, plates the all-plates arrange skipped and the job's notifications. An arrange may reorder objects, so list_objects again. One undo step.

align_y.description: Align to Y axis (off while rotate is on).

fill.description: Instead of arranging, fill this object's plate with more of it.

multi_material.description: Allow multiple materials on same plate.

commands.title: Arrange objects or fill the bed

commands.description: Slice the current plate, all plates, or one plate by index, the way the toolbar's Slice button does, and wait for the result (or reply with a job id when it takes longer than the reply budget). Each requested plate reports ok, error, cancelled, empty or skipped; the whole operation is superseded when someone else started a slice or edited the project while it ran. An ok plate has time_s (silent_time_s when the printer estimates it), filament_m and filament_g including flush, filament_cost, layers, max_z, filament_changes, and filaments[i] for slot i+1 with m, g and the grams of model_g, support_g, flush_g and tower_g. Other changes are refused until it finishes; cancel_job stops it.
commands.title: Slice

commands.description: Stop the running operation: a slice or G-code export, as the slicing progress's cancel button does, or a background job an MCP call started (an arrange, orient or fill bed). Its job then reports cancelled; a background job keeps other changes out until it has really stopped. With job, only that job is stopped: the running operation, a run_script run or an encode_recording. Allowed while an operation holds the project.

job.description: The operation's job to cancel, e.g. "j12".

commands.title: Cancel a job

commands.description: Replace an object's height range modifiers (Height Range Modifier in the object list): Z ranges in mm, each printed with its own layer_height, filament and process settings, starting from the object's layer height and filament. Ranges may touch but not overlap; [] removes them all. One undo step; the object is selected. Reply: the object's height and its ranges as list_objects shows them, and warnings, such as a variable layer height profile deciding the layer heights instead.

object_id.description: The id list_objects reports for this object: the call is refused when the index names another one now.

ranges.description: The object's ranges afterwards, in any order.

values.description: {key: value} as set_settings takes them: layer_height, extruder (0 = the object's filament) and per-region process settings such as sparse_infill_density or wall_loops.

commands.title: Set height range modifiers

commands.description: Run the Variable layer height panel's Adaptive, Smooth or Reset on an object, without opening the panel: adaptive computes layer heights from the object's shape (inside a height range, the range's layer_height), smooth smooths its profile (or the one its height ranges give), reset goes back to its layer height and ranges. One undo step; the object is selected. Reply: the object's height, its layer_height_profile {points, min_height, max_height} as list_objects shows it (absent after reset), and warnings.

keep_min.description: smooth: keep the minimum layer heights (default false).

object_id.description: The id list_objects reports for this object: the call is refused when the index names another one now.

quality.description: adaptive: 0 = quality .. 1 = speed (default 0.5, as the panel).

commands.title: Set a variable layer height profile

commands.description: Add or remove pauses, custom G-code, custom templates and filament changes at the start of a layer, as the Preview layer slider's menu does; they are saved per plate in the project. They go on the plate's sliced layers, so the plate needs an up-to-date slice, or must be the one the Preview still shows after an earlier edit; the call selects it and shows the Preview. Applies clear, then remove, then add, all checked first. One code per layer: a custom code or filament change where there is one replaces it. Not undoable, as in the slider. A change invalidates the plate's slice: slice again before exporting. Reply: the plate's codes as list_plates' layer_gcode lists them, each with z and layer.

add.description: Codes to add, each with layer or z.

filament.description: change_filament: printed from this layer up.

layer.description: 1-based, as the Preview's layer slider numbers layers.

z.description: mm: the layer whose top is at or above it.

clear.description: Remove every code on the plate first.

remove.description: Codes to remove, by layer or z.

layer.description: 1-based, as the Preview's layer slider numbers layers.

z.description: mm: the layer whose top is at or above it.

commands.title: Set custom G-code at a layer

commands.description: Capture what OrcaSlicer shows and return it as an image, downscaled to max_dim on the long edge (default 1280), plus the full-size PNG written to save_path (or the session's output folder). target: "main" (the main window), "canvas" (the visible 3D view exactly as rendered: scene, toolpaths, toolbars, ImGui panels; on the Design tab its view), "dialog" (the topmost modal dialog), or a ref: a window's from list_windows (one that is not modal, say), or a widget's from list_widgets, cropped to that widget (a page element's ref captures its whole web view). The result says when parts may differ from the screen (approximate). Point the view first with set_view.

include_image.description: Return the image itself (default true); false returns only the path.

max_dim.description: Long edge of the returned image.

save_path.description: Absolute .png path for the full-size image.

target.description: main (default), canvas, dialog, or a widget's ref or locator from list_widgets.

commands.title: Take a screenshot

commands.description: What the Preview shows for a sliced plate. summary: the slice reply's, plus prepare and travel time and travel distance. features: seconds, share of the print time and grams per feature type (the Line Type legend), and travel. layers: per layer (1-based, as set_view's layer) Z, height, seconds and grams, paged; layer_features adds each feature type's seconds. objects: grams per object instance, with its list_objects index when its name is unique. view, for the plate the Preview shows: view type, time mode, layer range, which legend rows are visible, and each view type's colour range for what the legend shows. Times are normal-mode estimates. A G-code file opened for viewing reads the same.

plate.description: Plate index; default the current plate.

commands.title: Get slice statistics

commands.description: Set up what the window shows, for screenshots and GUI work: the main tab, the 3D view (canvas: Prepare's, the preview or the assemble view, which has its own gizmos), the camera of the 3D view shown (a named direction, the default view, or fit to bed / objects / selection, then look_at, the point it looks at, an orbit to look from between the named directions, and the zoom), the preview's color scheme (picked as in the legend's combo, which shows every feature type again), legend rows, time estimate and layers (1-based, or up to a height). Only the given fields change. On the Design tab the camera points its view (default is its Home view; no fit_bed). The reply echoes them; preview layers as [first, last, count] with z, the heights of first and last; with any camera field, camera_state, the camera it leaves as get_app_state.camera gives it, and adjusted: ["zoom"] when the zoom was held to its limits.

canvas.description: 3D view: Prepare's, the preview, or the assemble view (needs an object; leave it with 3d, as its Return button does).

layer.description: Preview: show layers up to this one (1-based).

layer_z.description: Preview: show layers up to the first whose top is at or above this height (mm), as the slider places a custom G-code.

legend.description: Preview: show (true) or hide (false) legend rows: feature types by name as get_slice_stats lists them ("Sparse infill"), and travel, wipe, retract, unretract, seams, filament_changes, color_changes, pauses, custom_gcode, in any case and with _ or a space between words. Hiding a row this print lacks does nothing. Applied after view_type.

look_at.description: [x, y, z] in mm: the point the camera looks at, in the 3D view's world coordinates, as list_objects gives positions; on the Design tab, the Design view's, which the Design commands' world points use (describe_scene's modeling_origin is the sketch planes' origin). The camera moves parallel, keeping its direction and distance. After camera.

orbit.description: [yaw, pitch] in degrees: move the camera around what it looks at, yaw to its right and pitch up (negative looks from lower), after camera and look_at. The same on every install, unlike a mouse drag.

time_mode.description: Preview: the time estimate the legend and layer times show; silent only when the print has its own.

zoom.description: Screenshot pixels per mm at look_at's depth, so everywhere in an orthographic view; held to the camera's limits (at most 250, at least what the scene's size allows). Applied last.

commands.title: Point the view

commands.description: Replay a list of tool calls in order and report each step: {orca_replay:1, name, vars, steps:[{tool, args, expect, optional, await, save_as, timeout_s}]}, JSON with comments. Strings may use ${replay_dir}, ${out_dir}, ${env:NAME}, ${vars.NAME} and ${jobs.NAME}. A step that returns a job is awaited unless await:false, which stores the job under save_as so later steps can answer the dialog it opened. expect maps a JSON pointer into the step's result to matchers (eq ne gt ge lt le contains regex exists empty); the first failed step or expectation stops the run unless the step is optional. Writes result.json to out_dir (default: <replay name>.out next to a replay file). auto_answer_dialogs rules a replay registers end with it. export_replay turns this session into one.

out_dir.description: Absolute directory for result.json and screenshots; created if missing.

path.description: Absolute path of a replay file.

replay.description: The replay itself, as an object or as its JSON text, instead of path.

vars.description: Values that override the replay's vars.

commands.title: Run a replay

commands.description: Turn the calls this session made into a replay that run_replay runs: mutating calls, wait and screenshot, in order, with refs replaced by locators, job replies replayed with await:false, and screenshot paths moved under ${out_dir}. Calls that failed, at once or as a job later, are left out; so is a call whose job is still running (unless it waits on a dialog), which left_out_running lists as {tool, job}. Reply: the replay, which with path is also written there. clear:true starts a new recording afterwards.

clear.description: Forget the calls recorded so far once exported.

path.description: Absolute .json path to write.

commands.title: Export this session as a replay

commands.description: Run Python code inside OrcaSlicer as its main program (__name__ == "__main__") against orca.host, the whole plugin API (search_python_api searches it): read objects, meshes and settings, compute, use orca.host.ui and the preset API, and call these same tools, with their guards and undo, through orca.host.tools.call(name, args), from the code and from the threads and pool tasks it starts while the run lasts. Mesh and matrix arrays need numpy, which search_python_api says is installed or not; a file run's PEP 723 block can install it. The code runs on a worker thread, where calls documented as UI thread only raise RuntimeError. The run ends once its code and the non-daemon threads and pool tasks it started are done; its windows close with it. `args` holds the args you pass; set `result` to a JSON value to return it; print() output comes back as output. Reply: {status: finished | raised | cancelled | timed_out, result, output, traceback?, message?}; a script that raised changed what it changed before. The code's own file access is held to OrcaSlicer's folders (its data and resources folders, and for a file run the file's folder, read only), and it starts no programs or threads and reaches no network: such an access raises PermissionError, unless a person has let Python scripts run unrestricted in Preferences (get_app_state.python.scripts_unrestricted); the tools it calls work as they do for you. Recorded by export_replay as one step with its code, which a replay runs again against the project as it is then.

args.description: Bound to the name `args` in the code.

code.description: Python source, run as a module body.

filename.description: The name tracebacks show for the code (default <run_script>). An existing file's path makes it a file run, as `python file.py` runs it: __file__, sys.argv, imports from its folder and its PEP 723 dependencies; any other name only names it.

timeout_s.description: The run is stopped as timed_out after this many seconds (default 300).

commands.title: Run a Python script

commands.description: Search orca, the Python API of run_script scripts and plugins, in the running build: orca.host (the project's model and meshes, presets and their editors, slicing data, orca.host.ui windows and dialogs, orca.host.tools calling these tools) and the classes, events and pages plugins build on. Each entry has its kind, signature (a class's constructors) and documentation. A query ranks them, best match first; without one, the whole package is listed with each entry's first sentence. Page with offset. numpy says whether numpy is installed, which mesh and matrix arrays need.

commands.description: Record a video of OrcaSlicer until stop_recording: the main window with any modal dialog on it (target main), or the 3D view shown (canvas). Frames are MJPEG in a Matroska (.mkv) file with their real timestamps. With captions, the tool call acting on the app shows as a caption at the bottom (secret setting values never show); with pointer, the pointer is highlighted, its clicks rippling. Capture takes at most about a third of the UI thread, so the frame rate drops where capturing is slow. One recording at a time: one a replay or script starts ends with it, a client's when the server is turned off. With encode, the stop_recording that reports it also encodes it to an MP4 beside it, as the Start Recording command does; encode_recording makes an MP4 of any recording later. Called with no arguments, it opens the Start Recording dialog instead, as the Start Recording command does (blocked_by_dialog): its controls are named after their settings for set_widget_value, answer_dialog "Start recording" starts the person's recording, which neither the end of a replay or script nor the server turning off ends, and the dialog remembers the settings; silent: true starts one here at once with the defaults.

commands.description: Stop the running recording and return its file once it is written: seconds, frames captured and written, frames dropped when encoding fell behind, failed when they could not be encoded, or skipped when the window could not be captured, the size, the mean UI-thread time a capture took (capture_ms), and why it ended. A recording that ended on its own (max_seconds, the replay or script that started it ended, a write error) is reported once by the next stop_recording. For a recording started with encode, it then starts the MP4 encode and returns it under encode: a job, whose wait {for: "job"} returns encode_recording's result. This is the call with silent: true. Called with no arguments, it stops the recording as the Stop Recording command does, whoever started it: without waiting for its file, it shows the person a notification naming it and replies with its path; the next stop_recording with silent: true reports it as ended stopped_in_app.

commands.description:
Make a mouse gesture on a 3D canvas as a person would: move, down, up, click, drag or wheel. It starts at `at`, a point of the model, which is projected through the camera and by default checked to land on that part (check "point" only projects it), or at x/y, logical pixels from the canvas's top left. A drag goes through `waypoints` to `to`, `steps` moves per leg: on an object it moves the object, in a painting gizmo it paints from a press on the object being painted (waypoints zigzagging over an area paint all of it), and elsewhere it turns or pans the camera as this install's mouse settings say, so turn the camera with set_view camera or orbit instead. A wheel turns delta notches; positive zooms in or scrolls a panel up. Modifiers are held as keys for the gesture (shift for Measure's point picking, alt for erasing). A down keeps its button and modifiers held, so moves drag, until an up or another gesture. Grabbers are set through the gizmo's panel fields or transform, not dragged. A menu a right click opens is listed as popup_menu, or popup_item (with click or up) runs one of its items. The reply's camera_moved says the gesture moved the camera, so earlier screenshots and pixels no longer match the view.
With target, the gesture is on a web page's element instead (a canvas such as the colour picker's spectrum, a slider, a sortable or scrolled list): x/y, to and waypoints are logical pixels from its top left, a drag keeps the pointer captured where the page asks for it, and a wheel scrolls what is under the pointer unless the page takes it; page says what the gesture changed there, as for click.

commands.description: Answer modal dialogs automatically when their title or message matches a rule's regex (case-insensitive). get_app_state.auto_answer_rules lists the rules in force. Called from a replay or script, the rules last until it ends; otherwise they replace the ones this session set before, and an empty list clears them. A native dialog returns the rule's button at once and never shows. A file or folder picker takes button ok with an absolute path and returns it without showing (on Linux such a rule cancels it); without a path a picker can only be cancelled, and a multi-select picker takes no path. A wx dialog has the button pressed as answer_dialog does, so its handler runs. A matching dialog already open is answered too (answered_open_dialog), so a prompt that shows around the same time, such as the restore prompt after startup, is caught either way. A web dialog is matched by its title: a button that names one of its shown wx buttons (by label, standard name or id) is pressed as for a wx dialog, any other on its page once it shows there, for up to 10 s after the page loads; past that, cancel and close end the dialog and any other button gives up.

path.description: Absolute path a matching file or folder picker returns, with button ok. A picker has no title until it shows, so the rule matches its prompt and must not anchor on a title with ^. A picker the path can't serve is cancelled and the reason logged.
